name: haematology_2ww
document_description: a GP referral letter for the urgent suspected-cancer (two-week-wait) haematology pathway
domain_prompt:
Domain rules:
- Dates: DD/MM/YYYY. NHS number: 'XXX XXX XXXX' with spaces. UBRN: 'XXXX-XXXX-XXXX'.
- address / practice_address: street address only, WITHOUT the postcode (postcode goes in its own field). Hb is a number only (no units).
- The condition flags (leukaemia, lymphadenopathy, myeloma, splenomegaly) are the ticked suspicion boxes on the referral; suspected_pathway is the named suspected condition (e.g. 'myeloma', 'acute leukaemia').
- symptoms and myeloma_features are lists of the individual items stated, using the letter's own wording (e.g. 'Itching', 'Bruising/Bleeding', 'Renal impairment').
- discussed_with_patient: 'Y' or 'N'.

sex.description: 'M' or 'F'. If not stated explicitly, infer from title (Mr/Mrs/Ms/Miss) or wording like 'this gentleman'/'this lady'.

trust.description: The NHS trust that operates the destination hospital. If the letter names only the hospital, give that hospital's official NHS trust name from your knowledge (e.g. Homerton University Hospital -> 'Homerton Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust', St Bartholomew's Hospital -> 'Barts Health NHS Trust').

suspected_pathway.description: The suspected 2WW pathway, exactly one of: 'myeloma', 'acute leukaemia', 'chronic myeloid leukaemia', 'lymphoma', 'lymphoproliferative disorder', 'unexplained splenomegaly'. Map the letter's wording to the closest of these (e.g. 'CML' -> 'chronic myeloid leukaemia', 'unexplained persistent splenomegaly' -> 'unexplained splenomegaly').

leukaemia.description: true ONLY if this condition is explicitly marked/ticked as suspected on the referral, or explicitly named as the suspected diagnosis. Never infer from symptoms or clinical picture alone.

lymphadenopathy.description: true ONLY if this condition is explicitly marked/ticked as suspected on the referral, or explicitly named as the suspected diagnosis. Never infer from symptoms or clinical picture alone.

myeloma.description: true ONLY if this condition is explicitly marked/ticked as suspected on the referral, or explicitly named as the suspected diagnosis. Never infer from symptoms or clinical picture alone.

splenomegaly.description: true ONLY if this condition is explicitly marked/ticked as suspected on the referral, or explicitly named as the suspected diagnosis. Never infer from symptoms or clinical picture alone.

hb.description: Haemoglobin in g/L, number only, e.g. '102'

symptoms.description: ONLY the items given in the letter's explicit symptom list (e.g. after 'Symptoms:'), verbatim. Do not add symptoms mentioned elsewhere in the narrative; empty list if no explicit symptom list.

myeloma_features.description: Only items explicitly listed as myeloma features on the referral form. Do not infer from the narrative; empty list if none are listed.

investigations.description: Investigation results done or requested (blood film, repeat FBC, B12/folate, U&E, LDH, imaging, virology, CRP), plus directly related current status such as 'No antibiotics currently'. EXCLUDE the overall clinical-suspicion statement (e.g. 'The film/FBC is concerning for...') and past medical history.

medical_history.description: Past conditions, regular medications and allergies (including e.g. 'NKDA', 'Allergic to codeine'), verbatim and complete.

comments.description: The referrer's distinctive remarks only: patient-specific concerns, urgency observations, discussions with specialists, family history worries. EXCLUDE the clinical-suspicion statement ('Clinical picture is consistent with...', 'The film/FBC is concerning for...' — already captured by suspected_pathway) and standard boilerplate: 'The referral has (not) been discussed as an urgent suspected cancer referral', 'Please contact me on ... if further information is needed', greetings and sign-offs. Empty if nothing distinctive remains.

discussed_with_patient.description: 'Y' or 'N'. In narrative letters, 'The referral has been discussed as an urgent suspected cancer referral' means 'Y'; 'has not been discussed' means 'N'.
